items.title: Russia and Belarus sign new foreign policy coordination programme
items.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry announced that the two countries signed a foreign policy coordination programme for 2027–2029 following talks in Gomel. The programme will be submitted to the Union State's Supreme State Council for approval.

items.title: Lithuania sees no immediate need to close Russian border crossings
items.summary: Lithuanian border service chief Donatas Škarbonis reportedly said that current circumstances do not warrant closing border crossing points with Russia.

items.title: Russia claims strikes on Ukrainian defence industry and cargo vessel
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said overnight strikes hit Ukrainian defence industry facilities in Kyiv and a cargo vessel in the Black Sea that it alleged was carrying military and dual-use goods. The claims have not been independently verified.

items.title: Russia begins compensation payments for war-related equipment damage
items.summary: Russia's Finance Ministry said construction equipment owners have begun receiving compensation for war-related damage under a scheme covering Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories, including Crimea.

items.title: Russian regional authorities report civilian injuries following drone attacks
items.summary: Krasnodar regional authorities reported four people injured in the Slavyansk district, with two hospitalized. Belgorod's governor separately reported one civilian death and 14 injuries over the preceding day.

items.title: Russia claims 343 Ukrainian drones intercepted overnight
items.summary: Russian reports said air defences intercepted 343 Ukrainian drones overnight across multiple Russian regions, occupied Crimea and surrounding waters. The figure has not been independently verified.

items.title: Electricity largely restored in Russian-occupied Donetsk region
items.summary: Russian-appointed energy authorities said repairs had restored electricity across most of the territory they administer. Local outages remained in Donetsk and nine municipal districts.

items.title: Ukraine checks university enrolments linked to mobilization deferrals
items.summary: Deputy Education Minister Trofimenko said universities were being checked to establish whether male students over 25 who received deferrals were genuinely studying and whether institutions complied with enrolment rules.

items.title: Britain reportedly updates strategic reserve readiness records
items.summary: Reports indicate the British Ministry of Defence is updating information about military veterans who could be recalled in exceptional circumstances. Veterans Minister Kelvin Bailey stressed that the initiative did not indicate imminent mobilization.

items.title: Kremlin says invitation for European representatives to visit Moscow remains open
items.summary: Russian presidential aide Yuri Ushakov said Moscow had received various public statements but no formal European rejection of its invitation to visit the Russian capital.

items.title: SAPO announces recovery of 909,600 hryvnias in unjustified income
items.summary: Ukraine's Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office said the High Anti-Corruption Court's appeals chamber upheld the recovery of 909,600 hryvnias from a former Justice Ministry regional official and a relative. The case concerns proceeds from the resale of a vehicle previously subject to a confiscation ruling.

items.title: Russian aerospace forces deputy commander reportedly arrested
items.summary: Reports say a Moscow military court ordered the detention of Colonel General Yuri Grekhov, deputy commander of Russia's aerospace forces responsible for armaments, following a request from military investigators. The reported charges remain unknown and the detention has not been independently confirmed.

items.title: Russia reports evacuation of civilians from Kostiantynivka
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces evacuated another 16 civilians from Kostiantynivka and provided assistance to injured people. The account has not been independently verified.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange remains of fallen servicemen
items.summary: Russian State Duma deputy Shamsail Saraliev reported an exchange involving the remains of 250 Ukrainian and 22 Russian servicemen. The figures do not establish overall battlefield losses.

items.title: Germany reportedly seeks safeguards for future EU funding of Ukraine
items.summary: According to a report citing the Financial Times, Germany wants future financial support for Ukraine embedded in EU budget legislation to make it harder for individual member states to block funding. No final agreement was reported.

items.title: Ukraine's Supreme Court upholds confiscation of nearly 5.8 million hryvnias in assets
items.summary: Ukraine's Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office said the Supreme Court upheld the confiscation of unjustified assets used by a former local council chairman in Rivne region. The assets include residential property, land, a boat and a vehicle. The ruling is final.

items.title: Armenia plans gradual transfer of border protection to national forces
items.summary: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said Armenia intends to assume full responsibility for its borders in the coming years, gradually replacing Russian border guards. He also expressed a desire to resolve outstanding bilateral issues with Moscow.

items.title: New damage to energy infrastructure reported in Kharkiv
items.summary: Reports described renewed strikes affecting an aviation institute and an energy facility in Kharkiv. The city's mayor reportedly confirmed damage to an energy facility; the full extent of the damage remains unclear.

items.title: Power outages reported across Crimea and Sevastopol
items.summary: The electricity provider Krymenergo said outages in Russian-occupied Crimea were caused by failures outside the peninsula. Restoration work was underway. The cause of the initial failures was not specified.

items.title: Germany and Ukraine reportedly agree to cooperate on DELTA military software
items.summary: The two countries' defence ministers reportedly signed a declaration of intent on joint development and use of Ukraine's DELTA situational awareness system. Norway has also reportedly agreed to test the software. The reported arrangements do not establish direct German access to Ukrainian operational data.

items.title: Russia claims 872 Ukrainian drones intercepted over 24 hours
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry reported intercepting 872 Ukrainian drones over the preceding day and claimed strikes on Ukrainian unmanned-system production and storage facilities. The figures and strike results have not been independently verified.

items.title: Georgia proposes alternating venues for talks with Russia
items.summary: Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze expressed support for talks between Georgian and Russian representatives, proposing that meetings alternate between Moscow and Tbilisi.

items.title: Ukrainian paper products manufacturer reportedly halts production
items.summary: Reports say Ukrainian manufacturer Bloomi is discontinuing production across its brands, including Snizhna Panda, after repeated Russian strikes reportedly destroyed its production facilities and equipment. The extent of the damage has not been independently verified.

items.title: Russian-appointed Luhansk authorities report civilian casualties
items.summary: Russian-appointed regional head Leonid Pasechnik reported four deaths and eleven injuries from alleged Ukrainian attacks over the preceding day, alongside damage to civilian and energy infrastructure. The account has not been independently verified.

items.title: Fire reportedly continues at Kyiv industrial plant
items.summary: Reports describe a continuing fire at the Kyivkhimvolokno industrial plant following Russian strikes. The extent of damage and any environmental consequences remain unconfirmed.

items.title: Putin orders anniversary celebrations in occupied Berdiansk
items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree providing for celebrations in 2027 marking the 200th anniversary of the founding of Berdiansk, a Ukrainian city under Russian occupation.

items.title: New damage to critical infrastructure reported in Kryvyi Rih
items.summary: A Russian military correspondent reported renewed explosions in Kryvyi Rih, citing local authorities as confirming a strike on critical infrastructure. The extent of the damage remains unclear.

items.title: Ukrainian media reports allegations of military corruption
items.summary: Ukrainian outlet Strana reportedly interviewed soldiers from several units who alleged bribery for transfers away from combat, unofficial payments to commanders and misappropriation of military fuel. The allegations have not been independently verified.

items.title: Moscow issues warning to Western companies supporting Ukrainian attacks
items.summary: Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova warned that employees of Western companies assisting Ukrainian attacks on Russia could face criminal prosecution and claimed they could become military targets. That claim does not itself establish their status under international humanitarian law.

items.title: CSTO discusses military logistics modernization
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said a conference in Saint Petersburg examined modernization of the alliance's collective logistics system through 2040, drawing on experience from recent armed conflicts and considering greater use of automated systems.

items.title: Russian-appointed Horlivka mayor reports civilian death
items.summary: Ivan Prikhodko, the Russian-appointed mayor of occupied Horlivka, reported that a civilian had died in an alleged Ukrainian attack. The account has not been independently verified.

items.title: Trump expresses optimism about Ukraine peace negotiations
items.summary: US President Donald Trump reportedly described a near-term agreement to resolve the Russia–Ukraine war as entirely possible. No finalized agreement was announced.

items.title: Moscow denies allegations of plans for nuclear weapons in space
items.summary: Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova rejected German media reports alleging that Russia plans to deploy a nuclear weapon in orbit. She accused Germany of seeking justification for its own space weapons plans. The competing allegations have not been independently verified.

items.title: Russia reports further Ukrainian drone interceptions
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said air defences intercepted 34 Ukrainian drones during the day over Russian regions and the Black Sea and Sea of Azov. The figure has not been independently verified.

items.title: Russian ambassador outlines efforts to diversify agricultural export routes
items.summary: Russian Ambassador Roman Ambarov said Moscow is developing alternative agricultural export corridors, including Arctic routes, amid disruptions to Black Sea shipping. He also advocated establishing a BRICS grain exchange and expanding agricultural cooperation with African countries.

items.title: Putin approves Arctic development and security strategy
items.summary: Russia's new Arctic strategy identifies NATO's growing military presence as a security concern and sets a target of 110–150 million tonnes of annual Northern Sea Route cargo traffic by 2035. Putin instructed the government to develop a comprehensive Arctic development and transport project within six months.

items.title: Ukraine reportedly orders verification of military registration records
items.summary: Ukraine's cabinet has reportedly instructed authorities to verify military registration information for men aged 17 to 60. The Defence Ministry is expected to receive information from government registers, including identity, residence and citizenship records.

items.title: Lavrov argues West must negotiate rather than dictate sanctions policy
items.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov argued that Western countries would remain important international actors but would increasingly have to negotiate with other countries rather than dictate their foreign relationships and sanctions policies.

items.title: EU reportedly faces €100 billion in Ukraine loan expenditure
items.summary: A report citing an unnamed source puts anticipated EU expenditure on loans for Kyiv over the next seven years at €100 billion. The available report does not establish that a final funding agreement has been reached.

items.title: Russia claims strike on Ukrainian drone facility
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces destroyed a Ukrainian drone control and storage facility in the Dnipropetrovsk direction. The claimed result has not been independently verified.
